name: Philip Glass
hook: A minimalist composer who, fifteen years after Bowie and Eno borrowed from minimalism, turned their album 'Low' into a symphony.
blurb: Philip Glass was born in Baltimore in 1937. The Philip Glass Ensemble, formed in 1968, played amplified electric organs and wind instruments at rock volume, and he wrote for it music of short patterns that repeat and change slowly. 'Einstein on the Beach' (1976), an opera made with Robert Wilson, made his name. On this map he matters for a return trip. Minimalism had influenced David Bowie and Brian Eno's album 'Low' (Eno's own route to it ran through minimalism; see e-reich-eno). In 1992 Glass wrote his first symphony, premiered in Munich on 30 August, on themes from three pieces associated with 'Low', 'Subterraneans', 'Some Are' and 'Warszawa', and his Symphony No. 4 (1996) did the same with '"Heroes"'. So the influence came back the other way. Glass has said he let Bowie and Eno's ideas shape how he worked on the symphony.

signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The opera with Robert Wilson. Amplified organs and counting voices, nearly five hours long.
